item.title: The Arts Guild of Sonoma Presents: Thanks to Art — Wed Nov 4, 5:00 PM — Arts Guild of Sonoma
item.description:
**“Thanks to Art” at the Arts Guild of Sonoma | November 4–30**
Celebrate the creativity of local artists at the Arts Guild of Sonoma’s November exhibition, “Thanks to Art.” Featured Member Artist Susan Heeringa-Pieper presents imaginative mixed-media works, while Guest Artist Rebecca Plachte-Zuieback showcases intricate textile collages created from reclaimed fabrics. Discover original paintings, sculpture, ceramics, jewelry, photography, and more. Voted People's Choice Best Gallery. The Arts Guild of Sonoma is a cooperative gallery showcasing the work of its member artists alongside selected guest artists and special features. With a continually changing collection and a wide range of media and price points, the Guild offers an ongoing opportunity to discover original art in Sonoma.
**Opening Reception:** Saturday, November 4, 5–7:30 PM. Free and open to the public.
**Location:** 140 East Napa Street, Sonoma. Open Wednesday–Monday, 11 AM–5 PM. Free admission.

item.title: Marin Farmers Markets — Thu Nov 5, 8:00 AM — Marin Veterans' Memorial Auditorium
item.description:
Price: Free
Sponsor: Marin Center
Explore the bounty of summer at the Marin Farmers Markets. Taste vine-ripened tomatoes, corn that was picked that morning, and peaches so juicy you have to bend over just to get a bite. Farm-fresh eggs, grass-fed beef, artisan c heeses, raw milk, and freshly baked breads complete the shopping exper ience. Specialty prepared foods and handmade art add to the magic of the market.
Enjoy the intimate feeling of the Thursday Marin Farmers Market, an ideal place to meet for lunch and pick up fresh produce for the weekend. Discover the abundance and diversity of product at the celebrated Sunday Marin Farmers Market, the third largest farmers market in California. Turn your dollar into a vote for local sustainable agriculture, shrink your eco-footprint, and revive the feeling of being intimate ly connected to your food by meeting your farmers face-to-face. The market takes place rain or shine.
www.aginstitutemarin.org
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Dem

item.title: Introduction to Drawing Portraits From Photos (3 Session Class) — Wed Nov 11, 6:00 PM — Sebastopol Center for the Arts
item.description: Introduction to Drawing Portraits from Photos November 4th, 11th, and 18th 6:00-9:00pm $150.00 + $15.00 Materials Fee = $165.00 Age Restricted to 18+ About this class: In this three week course, students will learn and practice observational skills and fundamental drawing techniques while learning the basics of drawing portraits from photographs. Drawing human faces requires the same basic drawing skills that one employs for any subject – observing proportion, flattening shapes, and utilizing line or value to convey volume. But the conceptual weight of human faces tends to intimidate artists. When drawing any subject, the hardest skill is simply learning to see, a skill that anyone can be taught, practice, and hone. This course will focus on the practice of looking, and discovering strategies to find objectivity when rendering portraits. item.title: Paint & Sip with Genevieve Elkin — Fri Nov 13, 5:30 PM — Petaluma Arts Center
item.description:
Join us for a relaxed and social paint & sip evening. You'll be guided step-by-step through painting a scenic view using acrylics, with plenty of room to make it your own.
Whether you follow along or add your own creative twist, the focus is on enjoying the process and having fun. Sip on a beverage, come with friends or meet new ones, and settle into a laid-back night of painting and connection. No experience needed - just show up and create.
Genevieve Elkin was Born and raised in Mill Valley, California and is a multidisciplinary artist now based in Petaluma. She earned a BFA in Illustration from Parsons School of Design and has professionally managed art departments, supporting artists and new media on high-profile projects. Genevieve loves painting, drawing, and exploring ceramics, and enjoys helping students experiment, have fun, and develop their own creative voice.

item.description:
Join the Laguna de Santa Rosa for Laguna Stewards Day a fun and meaningful way to volunteer while enjoying the outdoors. We will be meeting at the parking lot at Shiloh Ranch Regional Park. We will be walking up to the pond where we will be planting native plants and removing invasive plants. This is a great way to get to know your community while stewarding this amazing site. We suggest wearing layers as it may be cold in the morning, long pants, closed-toe shoes, and sun protection. Bring a backpack, and a water bottle; we’ll bring the tools, gloves, extra water, and snacks. Only heavy rain cancels. All Ages are welcomed.

item.title: Write & Collage: Words, Images & Memory — Sat Nov 14, 10:00 AM — Petaluma Arts Center
item.description:
Join Marlene Cullen for a creative two-hour experience that brings writing and collage together. In the first hour, guided freewriting prompts invite you to explore memorable moments, stories, and experiences in a welcoming, supportive environment. In the second hour, transform those reflections into a visual expression using images, colors, and textures.
No writing or art experience is necessary—just bring your curiosity and a willingness to explore.
Bring: A notebook and pen. Collage materials will be provided, and you're welcome to bring a favorite poem, magazines, photographs, or other materials you'd like to incorporate.
Marlene Cullen is the founder of Writers Forum and creator of Jumpstart Writing Workshops. Through her website and blog, The Write Spot, she shares resources and inspiration to help writers discover and develop their voices.
The Write Spot anthologies edited by Marlene are collections of short stories, poems, and vignettes with prompts to encourage writing.
